questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A data engineering team scores a 40 GB file of sensor readings that already sits in Amazon S3. The results are needed for the morning batch report, and no user is waiting for an answer. Which type of inferencing fits this workload?
options: Real-time inferencing against a persistent REST endpoint
Asynchronous inferencing with an SNS notification for each request
Batch inferencing run as a transform job over data at rest
Serverless inferencing that scales to zero between calls
questions.explanation: Batch inferencing processes large volumes of data that are already at rest when nobody is waiting, so results can be written to S3 for the morning report. Real-time and serverless options target interactive requests, while asynchronous inferencing serves individual long-running requests that need a callback.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: Which statement correctly describes how artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning and generative AI relate to one another?
options: Generative AI is a subset of deep learning, which is a subset of machine learning, which is a branch of artificial intelligence
Machine learning is a broader field than artificial intelligence because it includes rule-based expert systems
Deep learning is a branch of generative AI that trains only on labeled data
Every artificial intelligence system learns from data through gradient descent
questions.explanation: AWS describes these as nested fields: generative AI is a very advanced form of deep learning, deep learning takes machine learning one step further, and machine learning is one branch of AI. Rule-based systems are AI without machine learning, so the options that invert the nesting are wrong.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A churn model reaches 99% accuracy on its training data but only 71% accuracy on the held-out evaluation set. What does this gap indicate?
options: Underfitting, because the model has high bias and is too simple for the data
A well-fit model, because training performance is high
A labeling error that always raises evaluation accuracy
Overfitting, because the model has high variance and memorized the training data
questions.explanation: AWS defines overfitting as accurate predictions on training data that do not generalize to new data, which matches a large gap between the two scores. Underfitting instead shows low scores on both the training and the evaluation set.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A team is documenting its ML pipeline for a new analyst. Which statements about training, inferencing and model vocabulary are accurate?
options: Training is the process of fitting a model to data so that it captures patterns in those data
Inferencing is the act of applying a trained model to new data to produce predictions
An epoch is the number of samples the algorithm uses in each training iteration
Batch inferencing suits large volumes of data when latency of minutes or hours is acceptable
An algorithm is the learning procedure that consumes training data and outputs a model
Real-time inferencing is the best fit for a job that runs once a night over files in S3
questions.explanation: Training, inferencing, batch inferencing and the definition of an algorithm all match AWS wording, so the first, second, fourth and fifth statements hold. An epoch is one pass through the entire training dataset while batch size is the samples per iteration, and a nightly job over data at rest is batch work rather than real-time work.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A company is sorting its datasets before choosing an AWS service for each one. Which of these datasets are classified as unstructured data?
options: Customer support text documents
Audio recordings of phone calls
Product photographs uploaded by sellers
Tabular order records in a relational database
Daily sales time series stored as timestamps and values
questions.explanation: Text, audio and images are unstructured data that route to services such as Amazon Comprehend, Amazon Transcribe and Amazon Rekognition. Tabular records and ordered time series remain structured data, which is the territory of classical SageMaker jobs.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A generative AI assistant does more than produce a single response. It breaks a goal into steps, calls an internal API to fetch account data, reviews the result, and decides on the next action until the request is complete. Which concept best describes this system?
options: A supervised learning model that maps fixed inputs to predefined outputs
Agentic AI, because the system plans multi-step work and uses tools to act toward a goal
Batch inferencing, because the work runs unattended without user interaction
A rule-based expert system that follows a fixed decision tree written by programmers
questions.explanation: Agentic AI describes systems that plan steps, use tools or APIs, and act autonomously toward a goal rather than only generating one response. The other options describe prediction, scheduled scoring, or hardcoded logic, none of which involves planning and acting.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A robotics team trains a control policy by letting it act inside a simulator and then adjusting the policy from a numeric reward received after each action. Which learning type is being used?
options: Supervised learning, because each reward acts as a label for the action
Unsupervised learning, because the simulator produces no human annotations
Reinforcement learning, because an agent learns by trial and error to maximize cumulative reward
Semi-supervised learning, because only some simulator episodes are scored
questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning is defined by an agent that takes actions in an environment and learns from a reward signal to maximize long-term reward. Labels, missing annotations, and partially labeled data describe other paradigms rather than trial-and-error learning.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: An application submits large imaging studies for analysis. Each study can take several minutes to process, callers cannot hold an HTTP connection open that long, and the caller wants an Amazon SNS message when each result is ready. Which inference option fits best?
options: Asynchronous inferencing with a destination for success and failure notifications
Real-time inferencing against a persistent endpoint that answers within seconds
Batch transform over files that already sit in object storage
Serverless inferencing that returns every prediction synchronously
questions.explanation: Asynchronous inferencing is built for queued requests with large payloads and long processing times, returns an output location, and can publish success or error notifications to Amazon SNS. Real-time and serverless options require a synchronous response, while batch transform scores data already at rest.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A scoring application receives short interactive requests, but traffic is bursty and near zero for long stretches. The team wants no idle capacity cost and does not want to manage instances or scaling policies. Which option fits best?
options: A real-time endpoint backed by a provisioned instance that stays running between requests
Batch transform that scores the input files once each night
Asynchronous inferencing with a queue in front of every interactive request
Serverless Inference, which scales with traffic and charges only for actual use
questions.explanation: Serverless Inference targets intermittent or unpredictable traffic: SageMaker AI manages the infrastructure, scales the endpoint to zero when idle, and bills only for use. The other options keep capacity running, add minutes of latency, or target long-running requests.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A model is trained only briefly and still fails to capture the relationship in the data, returning poor results on both recent and historical records. What does this indicate, and what should the team do?
options: Underfitting; add informative features and reduce regularization so the model can capture the pattern
Overfitting; increase regularization and remove features so the model stops memorizing
Data leakage; delete the evaluation set and retrain on every available row
Label noise; switch to unsupervised learning so labels are no longer required
questions.explanation: AWS defines underfitting as high bias, where the model is too simple and returns inaccurate results on both the training data and the test data, and recommends adding features while decreasing regularization. Overfitting shows the opposite pattern, with strong training results and weak evaluation results.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: Project pitches often blur generative AI and traditional supervised models. Which difference between the two is correct?
options: A traditional supervised model creates new text and images, while generative AI only assigns labels
Generative AI produces new content in response to prompts, while a traditional supervised model returns a prediction such as a label or a number
Generative AI always needs a fully labeled dataset for each task, while a traditional model does not
Traditional supervised models can only process numbers, while generative AI can process any input type
questions.explanation: AWS defines generative AI as systems that create new content such as text, images, and audio from prompts, whereas a supervised model predicts an existing target such as a label or a continuous value. The other options reverse or overstate those capabilities.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A colleague asks what makes a network deep. Which description of neural networks and deep learning is correct?
options: A neural network is a database structure used to store training examples for later retrieval
Deep learning refers to training a model for many hours, regardless of its internal structure
A neural network is a layered structure of connected nodes inspired by the human brain, and deep learning uses many such layers
Neural networks can only be trained on labeled image data
questions.explanation: AWS describes deep learning as an AI method inspired by the human brain that processes data through multi-layer neural networks. Depth refers to the number of layers, not training duration, and neural networks are not storage structures.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A newly trained model fails on fresh records and on the very records it was built from. Which explanation fits?
options: The model has high variance because it memorized the training examples
The model is overfitting, so regularization should be removed to improve it
The model learned the underlying pattern but is being scored on noisy labels only
The model has high bias, meaning its assumptions are too simple for the data
questions.explanation: AWS defines underfitting as high bias: the model gives inaccurate results on both the training data and the test set because it is too simple. High variance and overfitting describe the opposite pattern, where training performance is strong and evaluation performance collapses.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A draft wiki page makes several claims about data types. Which of these claims are correct?
options: Labeled data pairs each example with a known target value, which enables supervised learning
Unlabeled data has no target column, so it can still support clustering and pattern discovery
Time-series data is ordered in time, so past observations can be used to predict future values
Image data is structured data because each pixel can be written as a number
Text is considered structured data because words follow a fixed grammar
Data is labeled only when it is stored in a relational database
questions.explanation: Labeled, unlabeled, and time-series data are defined by what the records contain and how they are ordered, which determines the modeling approach. Images and text are treated as unstructured data for service selection, and labels come from annotation rather than from storage format.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: An internal explainer about large language models and generative AI is under review. Which of these claims should be kept?
options: A large language model is a supervised classifier that returns one fixed label for every input
A large language model is a deep learning model trained on very broad text data and adaptable to many language tasks
Generative AI can only classify inputs into categories that were defined during training
Generative AI produces new content such as text, images, audio, and video from prompts
A large language model produces output one token at a time, conditioned on the prompt and context
Generative AI requires a separately labeled training set for every new task it performs
questions.explanation: AWS describes large language models as broad deep learning models that generate language, and generative AI as systems that create new content from prompts, produced token by token from the context. The remaining statements recast these systems as fixed-label classifiers, which describes traditional supervised learning instead.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A data scientist is matching each project to a learning paradigm. Which of these pairings are accurate?
options: Marking historical emails as spam or not spam from a labeled archive - supervised learning
Reducing 150 columns to a few principal components without any labels - supervised learning
Grouping customers into segments when no segment labels exist - unsupervised learning
Detecting fraudulent transactions from a labeled history of fraud and legitimate cases - unsupervised learning
Estimating house prices in dollars from labeled sales records - supervised learning
Training a delivery bot that improves only from the rewards it receives - unsupervised learning
questions.explanation: Supervised learning requires examples that carry known target values, which covers spam labels, price values, and labeled fraud history, while unsupervised learning works without labels, as in customer segmentation. The remaining statements attach the wrong paradigm to their data.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A publisher must decide which AI field handles each job. Which account of computer vision, natural language processing, and their place in AI is correct?
options: Computer vision and natural language processing are the same field because both read text that appears in images
Computer vision extracts information such as objects, faces, and scenes from images and video
Natural language processing focuses on understanding and generating human language
Speech recognition converts written text into audible audio for a listener
Natural language processing is a subfield of computer vision
Computer vision and natural language processing are branches used within the wider field of artificial intelligence
questions.explanation: Computer vision handles visual input, natural language processing handles human language, and both are fields within artificial intelligence rather than within each other. Speech recognition converts audio into text, not text into audio.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: Pair each AI term with its correct definition.
options: An input attribute the model uses when making a prediction
The artifact produced after an algorithm learns patterns from training data
Comparable and consistent outcomes across demographic groups
The known target value attached to a training example during annotation
questions.explanation: A model is the artifact trained from data, a feature is an input attribute, a label is the annotated target value, and fairness means outcomes remain comparable across demographic groups.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A fraud-review console must return a risk score within 150 milliseconds for every transaction an analyst opens, and traffic is steady around the clock. Which type of inferencing fits this workload?
options: Batch inferencing
Asynchronous inferencing
Real-time inferencing
Training inferencing
questions.explanation: The exam guide names real-time inferencing for interactive workloads that need consistent low-latency responses over sustained traffic; batch suits offline data and async suits long jobs that notify a caller.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A new analyst confuses two terms: the step-by-step procedure a training job executes to learn patterns from data, and the resulting artifact that later serves predictions in production. Which pair names them correctly?
options: Algorithm and model
Model and inference
Feature and label
Hyperparameter and parameter
questions.explanation: An algorithm is the learning procedure itself, while the model is the trained artifact it produces; inference is running that artifact, and features and labels are data concepts.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A platform team is documenting how agentic AI differs from generative AI for a training session. Which statements are correct?
options: Agentic AI plans steps toward a goal and takes actions through tools
Generative AI produces new content such as text or images from a prompt
An agentic system can decide its next action based on the result of a tool call
Agentic AI and generative AI are two names for the same category
Generative AI always operates autonomously in external systems without supervision
Agentic AI requires fine-tuning a custom model before any tool can be used
questions.explanation: The guide treats agentic AI as acting toward a goal with tools and decisions, while generative AI creates content; they overlap in practice but are distinct concepts, and neither requires fine-tuning to act.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: Before launching a training job, a team fixes the learning rate, the batch size and the number of epochs, while the optimizer adjusts millions of weights as data flows through. Which statement is correct?
options: The learning rate, batch size and epochs are hyperparameters, while the weights are parameters learned during training
The weights are hyperparameters because the team reviews them after training, while the learning rate is learned from the data
Both the weights and the learning rate are parameters learned automatically, so neither is chosen before the job starts
Hyperparameters are the outputs of inference, while parameters are the inputs to the training job
questions.explanation: Hyperparameters are chosen before training and control the process (learning rate, batch size, epochs), while parameters are the weights the optimizer learns from the data.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A team wants a single view that counts, for one classifier, the true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives from its latest evaluation run. Which tool gives them that view?
options: A receiver operating characteristic curve
A silhouette score
A confusion matrix
A cost-benefit table
questions.explanation: The confusion matrix tabulates the four outcome counts directly; a ROC curve plots derived rates across thresholds, a silhouette score measures cluster quality, and cost-benefit tables are not a standard evaluation output.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: A team is explaining how its dataset is divided before training begins. Which statements about the roles of the three splits are correct?
options: The training split is where the model's weights are fitted
The validation split guides choices such as when to stop and which variant to keep
The test split provides a final estimate on data the model never influenced
The validation split is used to update the weights, so it should be the largest split
All three splits can be drawn from the same few hundred examples as long as they are shuffled
The test split should be consulted repeatedly during training to catch problems early
questions.explanation: Weights are fitted on the training split, decisions such as early stopping use the validation split, and the untouched test split gives the final estimate; reusing examples across splits or consulting the test set during training produces optimistic numbers.

questions.subdomain: 1.1 - Explain basic AI concepts and terminologies
questions.question: Place the steps of one training iteration in the order the optimizer performs them.
options: Update the weights using the computed gradients
Deploy the model to a production endpoint
Run the current model on the batch to produce predictions
Compare the predictions with the known targets to compute the loss
Backpropagate the error so each weight receives a gradient
questions.explanation: Each iteration predicts, measures the loss against the targets, backpropagates the error to obtain gradients, and then updates the weights; deployment happens after training, not inside an iteration.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A bank must apply twelve regulatory rules to every loan application and produce exactly the same auditable decision each time the same inputs are submitted. What is the most appropriate solution?
options: Train a supervised classification model on historical loan decisions
Implement a deterministic rules engine that evaluates the twelve rules in order
Fine-tune a foundation model on the bank's past lending memos
Deploy a reinforcement learning agent that learns a policy from customer behavior
questions.explanation: When the requirement is a specific, repeatable outcome rather than a prediction, a rules engine gives the same auditable answer every run and costs nothing to train. A model would only approximate the rules and would introduce variation that a reviewer cannot reproduce.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A support organization wants a managed service that detects the dominant language, the sentiment, and named entities in incoming customer emails. Which service should it use?
options: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Polly
Amazon Translate
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explanation: Amazon Comprehend performs natural language processing tasks such as language detection, sentiment analysis and entity extraction on text. Transcribe converts speech to text, Polly converts text to speech, and Translate converts text between languages.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A retail group is prioritizing its AI investments for the next quarter. Which situations are strong candidates for AI or machine learning?
options: Routing millions of incoming support tickets to the right queue automatically
Scaling a decision that humans cannot apply consistently at current volume
Applying a fixed set of compliance rules that must return identical output on every run
Detecting fraudulent transactions from patterns in historical payment data
A workflow where the cost of collecting and labeling data exceeds the value of the prediction
Predicting customer churn from labeled historical account activity
questions.explanation: AI and ML add value by assisting decisions, automating repetitive classification and scaling beyond human capacity, which covers the first, second, fourth and sixth statements. A deterministic rules requirement and a case where data and labeling costs outweigh the benefit are both reasons to decline an AI project.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Match each business requirement to the managed AWS AI service built for it.
prompts: Detect the dominant language and sentiment of support tickets
Convert recorded call-center audio into time-stamped text transcripts
Build a text and voice assistant that resolves account inquiries through intents and slots
Translate product descriptions into several target languages
Generate natural-sounding narration for an e-learning course
options: Amazon Polly
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Lex
Amazon Translate
Amazon Transcribe
questions.explanation: Comprehend reads language and sentiment from text, Transcribe turns speech into text, Lex builds intent-based conversation, Translate converts between languages, and Polly turns text into speech.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A retailer wants a model that predicts a continuous dollar amount for the lifetime value of each customer, using labeled historical accounts. Which technique should the team select?
options: Regression, because the target is a continuous numeric value
Binary classification, because the target comes from customer records
Clustering, because customers must be grouped before any prediction is possible
Reinforcement learning, because the value changes over the customer lifecycle
questions.explanation: AWS states that a continuous target value means regression while a categorical target means classification. Grouping data without labels and reward-driven learning solve different problems.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A product team proposes a model that predicts which customers will cancel a subscription. There is no record of past cancellations, and there is no practical way to reconstruct those outcomes. What should the team do?
options: Train an unsupervised model, because it can predict cancellation without labels
Use a reinforcement learning agent, because it learns from user behavior instead of labels
Decline the predictive model for now, because there is nothing to train or evaluate against
Deploy a foundation model and ask it to guess the cancellation outcome for each customer
questions.explanation: A supervised prediction requires historical examples of the target outcome, so without observable cancellation labels the team cannot train or evaluate any model. The other options substitute a method that does not create the missing signal.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A streaming service wants ranked watch-next suggestions generated in real time for each viewer from that viewer's interaction history. Which managed service is designed for this?
options: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Personalize
Amazon Forecast
Amazon Comprehend
questions.explanation: Amazon Personalize is the recommendation service that builds real-time personalization from user, item, and interaction data. Amazon Forecast targets time-series demand, Transcribe converts speech to text, and Comprehend analyzes the meaning of text.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A logistics company receives scanned customs forms and needs key-value pairs and table cells captured into a database without manual re-keying. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Lex
Amazon Textract
questions.explanation: Amazon Textract extracts text, key-value pairs, and table cells from scanned documents. Comprehend analyzes the meaning of plain text, Rekognition analyzes images and video, and Lex builds conversational interfaces.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: An insurer must show a regulator the reasoning behind each premium quote, using structured risk factors and a fixed numeric output. Which approach fits best?
options: A traditional, interpretable machine learning model trained on the tabular features
A large language model prompted to write a short justification for each decision
A generative image model that renders each decision as a visual report
An unsupervised clustering model that assigns each applicant to a group
questions.explanation: When the output must be a reproducible decision with an auditable explanation on structured data, a traditional interpretable model is the better fit. A language model introduces nondeterminism and free-form output, and clustering does not produce a decision score.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A company is choosing between a traditional ML model and a foundation model for a production use case. Which factors favor the traditional model?
options: Deployment must run on modest compute with predictable latency and a stable cost per prediction
Only a stable pattern in existing labeled outcomes is needed, so a compact purpose-built model is enough
At the expected request volume, running a large generative model for every prediction would cost far more than a compact model
The system must draft varied open-ended marketing copy from short prompts
The team wants to change behavior through prompt edits alone, with no labels or training pipeline
The task requires reasoning across free-form documents and generating natural language answers
questions.explanation: Traditional models suit fixed compute and latency budgets, stable labeled data, and high request volumes where a compact model stays affordable, so those three factors push the choice away from a foundation model. Open-ended generation, prompt-only iteration, and reasoning over unstructured documents are strengths of foundation models.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Which of these describe practical applications of agentic AI?
options: A model returns a single predicted probability for each row of an uploaded spreadsheet
An assistant decomposes a refund request into steps, checks policy, calls an order API, and completes the action
A system plans a sequence of tool calls, evaluates intermediate results, and adjusts its next step toward a goal
A nightly job scores files already stored in object storage and writes the results back
An agent researches a task, selects tools to gather information, and decides when the goal has been met
A classifier assigns one of three fixed categories to each incoming record
questions.explanation: Agentic AI is characterized by planning multi-step work, using tools or APIs, and deciding subsequent actions from intermediate results toward a goal. Single predictions, fixed-label classification, and scheduled batch scoring involve no planning or tool use.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: How are the capabilities of Amazon SageMaker AI correctly described?
options: It provides managed infrastructure for training custom models built by your own team
It can host a real-time endpoint that serves predictions over a network API
It includes AutoML capabilities that can automatically evaluate candidate algorithms for tabular data
It converts stored call recordings into text transcripts
It returns sentiment and entity scores for plain text without any custom training
It can train models but cannot be used to deploy them for inference
questions.explanation: SageMaker AI covers the custom-model lifecycle from managed training and automated algorithm search to hosted inference endpoints. Speech-to-text belongs to Amazon Transcribe, sentiment and entities belong to Amazon Comprehend, and deployment is a core SageMaker capability.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Which of these describe a knowledge base or enterprise assistant application?
options: An assistant retrieves relevant passages from company documents and answers with citations to them
A model generates an unsourced paragraph from its own parameters with no reference to company content
Retrieval and answers are limited to content the requesting user already has permission to read
Users ask questions in natural language without knowing which repository holds the answer
A vision model labels objects in uploaded photographs using predefined categories
A translation service converts text into another language without retrieving anything
questions.explanation: A knowledge base application retrieves the organization's own content, grounds and cites the answer in retrieved passages, respects each user's permissions, and exposes scattered repositories through natural language questions. Unsourced generation, image labeling, and translation are different application types.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Which machine learning technique fits each of these project needs?
prompts: Approve, reject, or review each insurance claim from labeled claim history
Estimate how many spare parts a depot will need next month
Group documents by topic when no topic labels exist
Flag transactions that deviate from a customer's normal pattern with no fraud labels
options: Regression
Clustering
Classification
Anomaly detection
questions.explanation: A categorical decision from labeled examples is classification, a future quantity is regression, unlabeled grouping is clustering, and unlabeled deviation detection is anomaly detection.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: For each real-world application, identify the AI field it belongs to.
prompts: Reading the text on street signs inside a photograph
Summarizing a long contract into three bullet points
Captioning a live radio broadcast in real time
Producing a ranked list of movies for one viewer
Estimating next quarter's power consumption from hourly meter readings
options: Recommendation systems
Computer vision
Speech recognition
Natural language processing
Time-series forecasting
questions.explanation: Text inside an image is computer vision, text summarization is natural language processing, live captioning is speech recognition, viewer-specific ranking is a recommendation system, and future consumption from ordered readings is time-series forecasting.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Which AWS managed service delivers each of these capabilities?
prompts: Check whether a live selfie matches the portrait on an uploaded identity document
Detect and mask personally identifiable information in support text
Identify who spoke when and redact sensitive content in call recordings
Route low-confidence model predictions to human reviewers for audit
options: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Augmented AI
questions.explanation: Rekognition verifies faces in images, Comprehend detects and redacts PII in text, Transcribe separates and redacts speakers in audio, and Amazon Augmented AI builds human review workflows for model predictions.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A social platform must automatically flag violent or explicit imagery in user uploads before the images appear in feeds, without building its own vision model. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon Transcribe
Amazon Rekognition
Amazon Comprehend
Amazon Translate
questions.explanation: Amazon Rekognition provides pre-trained image and video analysis, including moderation labels; Transcribe, Comprehend and Translate handle speech, text and translation respectively.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Match each business need to the approach that fits it best.
prompts: Draft natural-language answers to open-ended patient questions
Estimate next month's demand from five years of labeled monthly sales
Group account holders into similar segments with no labeled outcome
Apply fixed published tax rates to income with zero tolerance for variance
options: Supervised regression
Deterministic rules with no model
Unsupervised clustering
Foundation model
questions.explanation: Open-ended text generation suits a foundation model, a labeled continuous target suits regression, unlabeled grouping is clustering, and a fixed computation is the guide's example of when a specific outcome rather than a prediction is needed.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A financial analyst wants to flag likely churn straight from a spreadsheet in Amazon S3, using a visual interface, without writing code or managing notebooks. Which service fits best?
options: Amazon Bedrock Agents
Amazon SageMaker Canvas
Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
Amazon Augmented AI
questions.explanation: SageMaker Canvas is the no-code visual interface for business users to build and use models from their own data; Ground Truth creates labeled training data, Augmented AI routes work to human reviewers, and Bedrock Agents runs foundation-model agents.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: A team is evaluating whether prebuilt AWS AI services fit its needs. Which statements about prebuilt AI services are correct?
options: They expose a specific capability, such as sentiment analysis or speech transcription, behind a managed API
Standard use cases work out of the box, with custom training optional for specialized needs
They can be combined in one workflow, such as transcribing a call and then analyzing the transcript
They require the customer to train and operate a custom model before the first call
They guarantee accuracy on the company's proprietary data without any evaluation
They only accept input once it has been formatted for a particular foundation model
questions.explanation: Prebuilt services deliver one specific capability per API call with no customer training required for standard use and can be chained into workflows; they do not require a custom model, cannot guarantee domain accuracy without evaluation, and take plain text, images or audio as input.

questions.subdomain: 1.2 - Identify practical use cases for AI
questions.question: Match each project to the kind of input data it depends on most.
prompts: Transcribing recorded team meetings into searchable text
Detecting damaged packaging in uploaded product photos
Flagging invoices likely to be disputed, learned from past cases
Scoring sentiment across open-text survey comments
options: Historical records with labeled outcomes
Images and video
Free-text documents
Audio recordings
questions.explanation: Each project is defined by what it consumes: spoken audio, visual uploads, past labeled cases for supervised learning, or free text for language analysis.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A product manager asks how to judge whether the new recommendation feature was worth building. Which measure is a business metric rather than a model performance metric?
options: Return on investment generated by the deployed feature
F1 score measured on the held-out test set
Precision of the classifier on the evaluation split
Recall of the minority class in the training data
questions.explanation: Business metrics such as ROI, cost per user, development cost and customer feedback answer whether the project is worth it, while accuracy, precision, recall and F1 answer whether the model is correct. A model can score well on F1 and still lose money, so ROI is the business-side measure.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Two months after deployment, the distribution of input data shifts and prediction quality degrades. What should the team do next?
options: Nothing, because the model was already evaluated on a held-out set before deployment
Delete the endpoint, since a deployed model cannot be updated once it serves traffic
Use monitoring to confirm the drift, then trigger a re-training pipeline on fresh data
Remove the monitoring alerts so that the production team is not interrupted
questions.explanation: Monitoring for drift feeds back into re-training, which is what turns the lifecycle into a loop rather than a line. Pre-deployment evaluation does not protect against data that changes after launch, and endpoints are routinely updated through a re-training and redeployment cycle.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these Well-Architected ML lifecycle phases in the order in which a team encounters them.
options: Model deployment for inference and prediction
ML problem framing
Business goal identification
Data processing, including collection and feature engineering
Model development, including training and evaluation
questions.explanation: The ML Lens starts with the business goal, then frames the ML problem, processes data, develops the model and finally deploys it for inference. AWS notes that the phases contain feedback loops, but no team should begin model development before the business goal and problem framing exist.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these stages of an AI/ML pipeline in the order they occur in a typical project.
options: Train the model on the prepared data
Collect raw data from S3 and other sources
Deploy the model to an inference endpoint
Perform exploratory data analysis and pre-processing
Evaluate the model on held-out data
questions.explanation: Data is collected first, explored and pre-processed, used to train the model, and then the model is evaluated on held-out data before any endpoint exists. Deployment follows only once evaluation shows the model is production ready.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A research team wants to start from a foundation model whose weights it can inspect, download, and fine-tune on its own infrastructure instead of pre-training a model from scratch. Which source of models does this describe?
options: Open-source pre-trained models, such as the ones SageMaker JumpStart makes available
A custom model trained from scratch on the team's own corpus
A managed API service that bills per request and never exposes model weights
A rules engine compiled from documented business policies
questions.explanation: Objective 1.3 names open-source pre-trained models and training custom models as the sources of models, and SageMaker JumpStart is the AWS hub of pre-trained open-source models. The managed API option describes a way to use a model rather than where the model came from.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: An application team has already trained its own ranking model and wants to expose it as an HTTPS inference endpoint inside its own VPC, with the team controlling the underlying compute and scaling. Which method of using a model in production is this?
options: Calling a managed API service such as Amazon Bedrock
Running a self-hosted API, for example a SageMaker real-time endpoint the team provisions and scales
Submitting a nightly batch job over files stored in Amazon S3
Fine-tuning the model on every incoming request
questions.explanation: Objective 1.3 lists managed API service and self-hosted API as the two methods for using a model in production, and provisioning your own endpoint for your own model is the self-hosted path. A managed API such as Amazon Bedrock serves models that AWS operates, and fine-tuning per request is neither supported nor economical.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: In a pipeline design review, the team asks which service should own the stage where raw records are cleaned, transformed, and split into training and evaluation sets. Which answer is correct?
options: Amazon CloudWatch, which raises alarms when endpoint latency breaches its threshold
Amazon SageMaker Model Registry, which stores model versions, metrics, and approval status
Amazon SageMaker Processing, which runs the transformation script in a managed container and releases the compute when the job ends
Amazon EventBridge, which matches scheduled events and starts workflows
questions.explanation: Pre-processing is the pipeline stage in question, and a SageMaker Processing job runs cleaning and transformation scripts against data in Amazon S3 with compute billed only while the job runs. CloudWatch and EventBridge belong to the monitoring and orchestration stages, and the registry belongs to model promotion.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Nobody on the team can reproduce the model that is serving production traffic, because the exact steps exist only in one person's notebook. Which MLOps fundamental does this failure most directly violate?
options: Experimentation, where every run is tracked and comparable
Model monitoring, where live traffic is compared with a baseline
Model re-training, where drift or a schedule starts a new training run
Repeatable processes, where the same code and data produce the same result
questions.explanation: Repeatable processes is the MLOps fundamental that requires a workflow anyone can re-run to the same result, which SageMaker Pipelines implements as a versioned definition. Monitoring and re-training address drift after deployment, and experimentation concerns comparing runs rather than reproducing one.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A spam filter is blocking legitimate customer email, and support tickets about missing messages are rising. Which metric should the team improve?
options: Recall, the share of actual spam messages that the filter catches
Precision, the share of flagged messages that really are spam
Training speed measured in epochs per hour
The number of input features used by the filter
questions.explanation: False positives lower precision, because messages the filter flags are not actually spam, so improving precision directly reduces legitimate email being blocked. Recall measures the opposite error, missed spam, and the other two options are not evaluation metrics at all.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Usage of a deployed assistant is growing quickly, and leadership wants one number that shows what the service costs to run for each active user. Which business metric answers that question?
options: Return on investment for the overall initiative
Development costs incurred before launch
Cost per user of running the service
Customer feedback scores collected after launch
questions.explanation: Objective 1.3 lists cost per user, development costs, customer feedback, and ROI as business metrics, and cost per user is the one that tracks ongoing spend as usage grows. The other three answer different questions: overall return, one-time build spend, and satisfaction.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A platform team wants new model versions blocked from receiving traffic until evaluation metrics and an approval are attached to the registered model version. Which MLOps fundamental is the team putting into practice?
options: Production readiness, where nothing deploys without evidence
Model monitoring, where production data is compared with the training data
Model deployment, where the trained model is placed behind an inference endpoint
Data preparation, where raw records are cleaned and transformed
questions.explanation: Production readiness is the MLOps fundamental that gates deployment on evidence, implemented with a Model Registry approval status such as pending manual approval inside a pipeline. Model monitoring watches live traffic instead of gating it, and deployment and data preparation are pipeline stages rather than MLOps fundamentals.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Which statements correctly differentiate the components of an AI/ML pipeline?
options: Training fits the model to prepared data, while evaluation scores it on held-out data it has not seen
Deployment makes the model available for inference, and monitoring then compares live traffic with a baseline
Data collection supplies the raw records, and feature engineering derives the model inputs from them
Exploratory data analysis runs before pre-processing so that data quality issues are understood first
Evaluation removes the need for monitoring once accuracy passes its target
Feature engineering happens after the model has been deployed to production
questions.explanation: Objective 1.3 asks candidates to differentiate pipeline components, and the four correct statements follow the documented order of collection, exploratory data analysis, pre-processing, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment, and monitoring. Monitoring continues after deployment by design, and features must exist before a model can be trained or scored.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: An operations lead is separating MLOps fundamentals from ordinary pipeline work. Which answers are MLOps fundamentals?
options: Experimentation, where every run's parameters and results are tracked and comparable
Scalable systems, where inference capacity grows with traffic and data volume
Managing technical debt, where unversioned notebooks and hand-tuned artifacts are replaced with versioned assets
Hyperparameter tuning of a model's internal architecture
Human labeling of training records by annotators
Replacing every rules-based process with a generative AI application
questions.explanation: The exam guide names experimentation, repeatable processes, scalable systems, managing technical debt, production readiness, model monitoring, and model re-training as the MLOps fundamentals. Hyperparameter tuning and data labeling are pipeline activities rather than MLOps fundamentals, and replacing rules with generative AI is not an MLOps practice.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: An architecture review pairs AI/ML pipeline stages with the AWS services that perform them. Which pairings are correct?
options: Pre-processing - a SageMaker Processing job cleans and transforms the raw records
Feature engineering - Amazon SageMaker Feature Store keeps offline and online feature data
Model training - a SageMaker training job runs the algorithm over the prepared data
Monitoring - Amazon CloudWatch alarms report drift and latency against a baseline
Evaluation - Amazon EventBridge matches events and starts workflows
Data collection - Amazon SageMaker Model Registry stores approved model versions
questions.explanation: Each correct pair maps a pipeline stage to the AWS feature the exam guide names for it: Processing for pre-processing, Feature Store for features, training jobs for training, and CloudWatch for monitoring alarms. EventBridge is an orchestration trigger rather than an evaluation stage, and the Model Registry stores model versions rather than raw data.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these steps of the automated re-training loop, from the first drift alarm to the updated endpoint, in order.
options: A CloudWatch alarm fires because captured production inputs have drifted from the baseline
An EventBridge rule matches the alarm and starts a new SageMaker Pipelines execution
The pipeline trains a candidate model on refreshed data and evaluates it on held-out data
The new version is registered with its evaluation metrics and set to await manual approval
A reviewer approves the version and it replaces the model currently serving traffic
The team stops sampling production traffic so that no further comparison is possible
questions.explanation: This is the canonical MLOps loop: captured traffic establishes a baseline, CloudWatch detects the deviation, EventBridge starts the pipeline, the registry holds the evaluated version until a human approves it, and only then does the endpoint change. Stopping traffic sampling would disable the monitoring that started the loop.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Sequence these staged model promotion steps, from validation on staging to the full traffic cutover.
options: Deploy the registered model version to a staging endpoint for validation
Shift a small percentage of live traffic to the new version
Compare latency and quality metrics between the old and the new version
Route all traffic to the new version once the comparison passes
Delete the previous model version before any traffic is shifted
questions.explanation: Promotion validates the version on staging first, then shifts a small share of live traffic, then compares metrics, and finally cuts over fully once the evidence supports it. Retiring the previous version first would remove the rollback path that the comparison depends on.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Sequence these steps to show how one feature travels from source records to a live prediction.
options: A processing job cleans and transforms the raw source records
Engineered features are written to the offline store as files in Amazon S3
A training job reads a point-in-time correct snapshot from the offline store
A real-time request reads the latest feature values from the online store and scores the row
Every inference request recomputes each feature from the raw source records
questions.explanation: Features are engineered and persisted in the offline store so training gets a point-in-time correct snapshot, and the online store then serves the latest values at inference time in single-digit milliseconds. Recomputing every feature from raw source data on each request would defeat the purpose of a feature store and could not meet a real-time latency budget.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Sequence these activities as a team works through one experimentation cycle for model improvement.
options: State the hypothesis and the metric that will decide whether it held
Run a tracked training experiment with its parameters and data version recorded
Compare the run's metrics against previous runs and the baseline
Adopt the winning configuration and feed it into the repeatable pipeline
Publish the unreviewed experiment notebook straight to the endpoint
questions.explanation: Experimentation starts with a stated hypothesis and a deciding metric, proceeds to a tracked run, then compares that run against prior runs, and only then adopts the winner into a repeatable pipeline. Shipping an unreviewed notebook skips tracking, comparison, and production readiness in a single step.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A screening model reviews claim documents for evidence of insurance fraud. Missed fraud cases cost far more than extra reviews, so the team must prioritize catching every actual case. Which metric should it optimize?
options: Precision
Accuracy
Specificity
Recall
questions.explanation: Recall measures how many of the truly positive cases the model found, which matches a cost structure where a miss is the expensive error.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A model team is reviewing how classification metrics behave on a heavily imbalanced dataset. Which statements are correct?
options: Accuracy can look high while the model misses most of the rare class
Precision answers: of the cases the model flagged, how many were truly positive
F1 score combines precision and recall into a single figure
The exam guide now lists AUC in place of F1 as a core metric example
Recall can only be computed when the model outputs probabilities instead of labels
On imbalanced data the guide recommends reporting accuracy alone
questions.explanation: Accuracy hides rare-class collapse, precision and recall describe opposite error directions, and F1 balances them; the current guide lists accuracy, precision, recall and F1, and both recall and precision are computable from a confusion matrix of labels.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place the steps of one data-labeling iteration for a supervised learning project in the order they occur.
options: Label the full dataset and audit a random sample for quality
Run a pilot labeling batch on a small sample
Deploy the model to production
Write the labeling instructions and define the classes
Revise the instructions where labelers disagreed
Measure agreement between labelers and identify disagreements
questions.explanation: Instructions come first, a pilot exposes ambiguity, an agreement measure quantifies it, revision fixes it, and only then does full labeling with a quality audit proceed; deployment belongs much later in the lifecycle.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: A logistics team forecasts daily demand in liters and must report the typical prediction error in the target's own unit while weighing a few large misses more heavily than many small ones. Which metric fits?
options: Root mean squared error
F1 score
ROUGE-L
Area under the ROC curve
questions.explanation: Root mean squared error stays in the target's units and, because errors are squared, large misses weigh more than small ones; F1 and area under the ROC curve are classification metrics, and ROUGE-L scores generated text against references.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Place these steps of five-fold cross-validation in the order the team performs them.
options: Average the five validation scores into one estimate of performance
Train the model on four of the five folds
Hold out the fifth fold as the validation data for that round
Deploy the model to production
Split the labeled dataset into five equal folds
Repeat the train-and-validate cycle so every fold serves as validation once
questions.explanation: Cross-validation splits the data into k folds, rotates one fold as validation against the other four for training, repeats until every fold has served as validation, and averages the scores; deployment comes only after evaluation.

questions.subdomain: 1.3 - Describe the AI/ML development lifecycle
questions.question: Match each phase of the AI/ML lifecycle to the main artifact it produces.
options: Drift and quality alerts on live traffic
A versioned endpoint serving predictions
A cleaned, versioned dataset ready for training
A trained model checkpoint with its configuration
Metrics on a held-out set with a go or no-go recommendation
questions.explanation: Each phase leaves a distinct deliverable: a ready dataset, a trained checkpoint, an evaluation report with a decision, a serving endpoint, and live alerts; confusing these makes it impossible to trace what produced the model in production.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A company runs a high-volume summarization workload on Amazon Bedrock and wants to understand what drives its bill. Which factor has the greatest direct effect on the cost of each request?
options: The number of concurrent applications sharing the account
The count of input tokens processed and output tokens generated
The size of the container image used to host the model
The number of developers with console access to the account
questions.explanation: On-demand foundation model pricing is metered per input and output token, so prompt length and generated length are the levers that move cost and latency together. Account activity, container size and developer counts do not change the token meter of a single invocation.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: During long conversations, a support agent bot gradually stops following its own operating instructions even though every request returns successfully. What best explains this behavior?
options: The tokenizer silently changed, so the same text now produces fewer tokens
A guardrail is blocking the instructions before they reach the model
The application is sending the requests to a different AWS Region
The context window is full, so the oldest tokens including the system prompt are evicted
questions.explanation: AWS describes the context window as a FIFO buffer: once it fills, each new token evicts the oldest one, and the system prompt is usually the oldest content. The call still succeeds, so behavior drifts instead of raising an error, a condition AWS calls context window overflow.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A developer wants agents built with different frameworks to reach the same external tools and data sources through one common standard. Which technology provides this?
options: Model Context Protocol
OAuth 2.0 authorization grants
OpenID Connect token exchange
Amazon S3 event notifications
questions.explanation: Model Context Protocol is the open standard that lets agents and AI applications connect to tools and data sources in a consistent way, and it is an explicit objective under agentic AI. OAuth, OpenID Connect and S3 notifications solve authentication and file events, not tool integration for agents.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is designing an agentic solution on AWS. Which capabilities are part of agentic AI as the exam defines it?
options: A supervisor agent that coordinates collaborator agents on a complex task
Managed memory that carries context across sessions for the same user
Runtime tool usage, where the model selects and invokes an API it needs
A guarantee that the agent will never produce an incorrect statement
Workflow orchestration in which the model decides the next step at runtime
Fixed, identical responses for every request without any reasoning steps
questions.explanation: Agentic AI covers multi-agent patterns, memory management, tool usage and workflow orchestration, which are the four capabilities listed here. Agents remain nondeterministic and fallible, so any option promising guaranteed correctness or fixed identical output is wrong.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Place these foundation model lifecycle stages in the order they occur.
options: Fine-tuning
Evaluation
Data selection
Pre-training
Model selection
questions.explanation: AWS defines the foundation model lifecycle as data selection, then model selection, then pre-training, fine-tuning and evaluation, with deployment and feedback following. Each stage builds on the previous one, so neither pre-training nor fine-tuning can start before the data and the model family are chosen.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Match each generative AI term to its definition.
options: Splitting a long document into smaller segments so each one fits a model's input limit
Designing and refining the instruction text sent to a model to improve its output
The unit of text a model reads and writes, produced by splitting input with a tokenizer
A generative model that creates new content by reversing progressively added noise
The maximum number of tokens a model can consider at one time
A dense numeric representation that places semantically similar items near each other
questions.explanation: A token is the model's unit of text, chunking splits long inputs into fitting segments, an embedding is a dense vector, the context window is the token budget for one call, prompt engineering is instruction design, and a diffusion model generates content by learning to reverse noise.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A marketing team wants a service that produces brand-new product illustrations from a written brief instead of retrieving existing artwork. Which generative AI use case does this represent?
options: Text-to-image generation
Sentiment analysis of customer reviews
Demand forecasting for inventory levels
Anomaly detection in payment records
questions.explanation: Image, video, and audio generation are the content-generation use cases the exam guide lists for generative AI models, typically implemented with a diffusion model behind a text-to-image API. The other three options are traditional ML tasks that label, forecast, or score existing records rather than create new content.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team asks why transformer-based language models handle long input sequences more effectively than recurrent networks. What is the best answer?
options: They store every training document verbatim and copy passages from memory
They reduce each input to a single fixed-size keyword before reading it
They read the sequence one position at a time and carry a hidden state forward
They process the whole sequence in parallel and let every token attend to every other token
questions.explanation: Transformers process the entire sequence in parallel using self-attention, which gives them faster training and the ability to handle much longer sequences than recurrent networks. Reading one position at a time with a hidden state describes the recurrent architecture that transformers replaced.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A support tool accepts a screenshot and a written question and returns a written answer. Which model type best describes this system?
options: A diffusion model that removes noise from an image over successive steps
An embedding model that returns only numeric vectors
A multi-modal model that accepts image and text input and produces text
A text-only large language model with a longer context window
questions.explanation: A multi-modal model accepts more than one input type, and the exam's modality table lists text-image-to-text models for exactly this shape. A diffusion model generates images, an embedding model returns vectors rather than answers, and a text-only model cannot read the screenshot.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: The exam guide describes the foundation model lifecycle as a cycle rather than a straight line. Which statement about that cycle is correct?
options: Feedback is gathered only before pre-training starts
Deployment is the final stage and no stage follows it
Evaluation happens once, before any fine-tuning is attempted
Feedback from the deployed model loops back into data selection for the next cycle
questions.explanation: The exam guide presents the foundation model lifecycle as a cycle of data selection, model selection, pre-training, fine-tuning, evaluation, deployment, and feedback, with feedback feeding back into data selection. Deployment is therefore a stage with a successor rather than an endpoint.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A ticket-classification prompt needs reliable output formatting on a simple task, and the team wants the smallest token increase that still controls the format. Which prompting approach fits?
options: Chain-of-thought instructions that ask the model to reason step by step
Few-shot prompting with three to five worked examples and the instruction placed at the end
Zero-shot prompting with an instruction and no examples at all
Self-consistency, sampling several reasoning paths and taking the majority answer
questions.explanation: AWS documents three to five examples as enough to control format on a simple classification task, with the instruction placed at the end of the prompt. Chain-of-thought and self-consistency add latency and output tokens that a simple formatting task does not need, and zero-shot gives the least format control.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team counts the tokens in the same policy document with two different Bedrock models and gets two different totals. What best explains the difference?
options: The two requests were billed at different token prices
Each model uses its own tokenizer, so the same text splits into different token sequences
One of the models silently discarded the middle of the document
Token counts differ only when the text contains characters outside the English alphabet
questions.explanation: Token counting is model-specific because different models use different tokenization strategies, which is why Bedrock exposes a CountTokens call that runs the selected model's tokenizer on the exact input. Pricing does not change counts, and no model truncates silently for a counting request.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A language model developer is reviewing what actually happens when a model reads text and compares meaning. Which statements are accurate?
options: Similarity between two embeddings is computed by the vector database rather than by the model
Chunking decides how much of a document reaches the model at once, which affects both token cost and relevance
A foundation model is adapted to new tasks through prompting or fine-tuning rather than retrained from scratch
Token counts always equal the number of words in the input text
The vector database creates the embeddings on demand, so no embedding model is involved
questions.explanation: An embedding model produces the vectors while the vector database performs the similarity search, chunking controls how much text enters the model and therefore both cost and relevance, and a foundation model is adapted through prompting or fine-tuning instead of retraining. Token counts do not match word counts, and embeddings come from an embedding model rather than from the database that stores them.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team's requests have become slow and expensive because every call carries the full policy manual, the entire chat history, and loosely related retrieval results. Which practices belong to context engineering?
options: Ranking retrieved passages and keeping only the most relevant ones
Budgeting tokens across the system prompt, the user input, the retrieved context, and the output
Summarizing older conversation turns instead of replaying them in full
Appending every retrieved document in full so that nothing is missed
Raising temperature so that the model explores a wider range of word choices
Setting the output token cap to the model maximum on every request
questions.explanation: Context engineering is the practice of deciding what enters the context window and what it costs, so re-ranking, token budgeting, and summarizing older turns all shrink the prompt while preserving relevance. Appending everything defeats that purpose, and temperature and output caps are generation settings rather than context selection.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Which changes reduce the token cost of an Amazon Bedrock workload without switching to a different model?
options: Setting the output token cap close to the typical answer length
Removing few-shot examples that add no measurable accuracy
Caching a long prefix that repeats across requests so it is not reprocessed each time
Sending only the top-ranked retrieved passages instead of the whole document
Adding chain-of-thought instructions to a simple routing task
Raising temperature to 1.0 so that responses are more varied
questions.explanation: Token-based pricing means cost follows input and output tokens, so tighter output caps, fewer unused examples, prefix caching, and leaner retrieved context all lower the bill for the same model. Chain-of-thought adds output tokens and latency, and temperature changes randomness rather than the number of tokens billed.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence the phases of one Amazon Bedrock agent invocation, from the incoming request to the streamed answer.
options: Post-processing formats the final answer, a phase that is off by default
Pre-processing validates the request and returns a validity rationale
The orchestration loop produces a rationale, predicts an action or knowledge-base query, and receives an observation
Answer chunks stream back to the calling application
The application installs a new foundation model into the agent's catalog
questions.explanation: AWS documents the runtime order as pre-processing, then the orchestration loop until an answer exists, then post-processing, which is disabled by default, and finally the streamed answer chunks. Installing models is a build-time concern and is not a runtime phase.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence one model-initiated tool call, from the outgoing request through to the final answer.
options: Your application sends the request with the tool definitions and their input schema
The model returns a tool-use stop reason together with a proposed JSON call
Your application executes the function and returns the result to the model
The model uses the result to produce the final natural-language answer
The model executes the function inside its own sandbox without your code
questions.explanation: With Converse tool configuration, your code supplies the tool schema, the model only proposes a JSON call, your application executes it, and the model turns the returned result into the answer. The model never executes the function itself, which is the boundary that defines raw tool use.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: Sequence one supervisor-based multi-agent interaction, from the customer question to the delivered answer.
options: A customer question reaches the supervisor agent
The supervisor selects one collaborator agent for the request
The collaborator runs its action group and returns a result
The supervisor synthesizes the result into a single answer for the customer
The collaborator becomes the entry point for every future customer question
questions.explanation: In supervisor with routing mode the supervisor stays the entry point, picks one collaborator, receives its result, and synthesizes the final answer for the customer. A collaborator never becomes the entry point, because clients always invoke the supervisor's alias.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each transformer concept, select the description that fits it.
options: What a token is searching for elsewhere in the sequence
Generating one token at a time, appending it, and running the model again
The label each token advertises about itself for attention scoring
Information injected so that the model knows the order in which tokens appear
The mechanism that lets every token weigh every other token in the sequence
questions.explanation: Self-attention scores every token against every other token using queries against keys, positional encoding supplies order because attention itself is permutation-invariant, and autoregressive decoding regenerates the sequence one token at a time.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each model concept, select the description that fits it.
options: A model that accepts more than one input type, such as an image plus a written question
An array of numbers produced by an embedding model and compared for similarity
A large model pre-trained on broad data and adaptable to many downstream tasks
AI that creates new text, image, audio, video, or code rather than only labeling data
A language model built from many stacked transformer blocks trained on broad corpora
questions.explanation: A foundation model is broad and adaptable, a multi-modal model takes several input types, a vector is the numeric output of an embedding model, a transformer-based large language model is a stacked-block architecture trained on broad text, and generative AI creates new content instead of only labeling data.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: For each generative AI use case, select the category it belongs to.
prompts: Drafting a condensed version of a long report
Creating a product illustration from a written brief
Translating a support article into another language
Answering customer questions in a chat window
options: Translation
Code generation
Summarization
AI assistant
Image generation
questions.explanation: These map directly onto the generative AI use cases the exam guide lists: summarization, image generation, translation, code generation, and AI assistants such as customer service agents. Each case produces new content rather than scoring or sorting existing records.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A design tool creates original images from written descriptions. Which generative technique underlies this kind of image generation?
options: Sequence-to-sequence translation of the input text
Clustering documents in embedding space
Diffusion models that iteratively denoise
A recurrent network that copies pixels from a reference image
questions.explanation: The exam guide names diffusion models as the technique behind image generation, where the model starts from noise and refines it step by step into an image.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A search feature must surface policy documents whose wording never contains the user's keywords but whose meaning matches the query. Which approach provides this?
options: Convert documents and queries into embedding vectors and search by vector similarity
Match exact keywords with a case-sensitive string comparison
Store the documents in a key-value store and look them up by document ID
Summarize every document into one sentence and compare text lengths
questions.explanation: Embeddings place semantically similar text near each other in vector space, so meaning-based retrieval works without keyword overlap; the guide pairs embeddings and vectors with exactly this role.

questions.subdomain: 2.1 - Explain the basic concepts of generative AI
questions.question: A team is splitting long documents into chunks before embedding them for retrieval. Which statements about chunking are correct?
options: Chunks that are too small can separate a sentence from the context it depends on
